anomalies.obs: On the root sheet (PCB.kicad_sch), the top-edge power pins of U2 (STM32L476RGT6) are wired to the VCC rail: junction dots join pins 21 (VDD), 43 (VDD) and 49 (VDDA) to the VCC arrow. However, the stub from pin 1 (VBAT) is marked with a red no-connect flag (X) at the point it crosses the VCC line, leaving VBAT floating — no other wire, battery, or diode connects to it anywhere on the drawing.
anomalies.exp: Standard STM32L4 practice (and the reference design) requires VBAT to be tied to VCC when no backup battery is present. The spec confirms no battery/regulator exists on the board ('no battery, regulator, or USB part appears anywhere'), so VBAT must be connected to VCC like the other VDD pins.

evidence.quote: Root sheet, top of U2: '1 VBAT' stub carries a red no-connect X at the VCC rail, while pins 21 VDD, 43 VDD, 49 VDDA have junction dots on the same VCC wire
no battery, regulator, or USB part appears anywhere in the three .kicad_sch files or PCB.net/PCB.cir

anomalies.impact: The MCU's VBAT/backup-domain supply pin is left unconnected, so the RTC/backup domain and the internal power-path for VBAT are unpowered; depending on the device this can prevent proper start-up, cause the backup domain to be unpowered, or produce undefined behaviour versus the intended VBAT-to-VCC connection.

parsed.summary: All buses, pull-ups, decoupling, TSC, NFC antenna and OLED charge-pump connections match the specification, but U2 pin 1 (VBAT) carries a no-connect marker where it should join the VCC rail (no backup battery exists on this board), leaving the VBAT pin floating — a deviation from the intended design.
